statement: On 33 fresh prime-order Weierstrass curves (group orders about 2^24, 2^28 and 2^32), T = 1024/4096/16384, 22 paired configurations per cell, counted F_p and mod-n operations (I = 3/10/30 M, S = M) with hash-table, solver and counted native operations (rho step-index hashes, distinguished-point canonicalisations and point hashes, IC offset-step indices) at 0/0.1/1 GAE each: the cheapest of four multi-target index-calculus variants (ic5, ic5ks, ic5w, ic5rw) per configuration and price is unranked against the cheapest of ten runs of this harness's multi-target rho (Kuhn-Struik retention rho rho2xks, distinguished-point rho rhodpu) in all 27 cell x I/M section-5a decisions, because the order flips with h: at I = 10M it costs 1.06-1.16x per target at h = 0 (dearer in all 9 cells), 1.00-1.05x at h = 0.1 and 0.71-0.80x at h = 1 (cheaper in all 9 cells); with native operations unpriced it is dearer in all 27; it is 1.11-1.47x a paired BSGS.
